column7: The essence of this match up is essentially dodging Aatrox's Q sweet spots, avoiding his passive and playing for short trades to whittle his health down. Eventually when fighting Aatrox, try to force fights when he is 50% HP, as this threshold will allow you to kill him or force him into a tower diving situation. This match up heavily relies on the ability to sidestep his abilities, while also utilising  healing reduction through ignite or executioners to help weaken his laning and mid game power. Building burst items through Eclipse, Cleaver or BoTRK also help stat check and provide the damage needed to help keep him behind. Within skirmishes and teamfights, try to avoid  Aatrox getting kills through his R, as he can use it to reset his CD and keep up his R timer. When fighting Aatrox solo, try to also use your R to help you have the necessary damage and stats to overpower him. Later on you can potentially build DD to help weaken his overall dueling power..
column8:
(1) Level 1 Q Start - Try to push for level 2 advantage while poking Aatrox with your Q, on level 2 skill E/W use advantage to chunk out Aatrox. Try to avoid tanking Aatrox’s Q damage in the process by using short in and out clicks to bait them out.

(2) Dodge Aatrox’s Q's - The biggest aspect towards overpowering and beating Aatrox is trying to avoid his Q sweet spots. Try to abuse short clicks against Aatrox, by clicking in and out very fast. We can essentially avoid Aatrox’s Q1 and Q2 from doing this alone, allowing us to hold our E for his Q3. Being able to dodge Aatrox Q's is necessary in being able to win the match up. Be aware his CD will drastically lower through the game, so ensure that you remain confident with your movement to help avoid Aatrox’s overall threat level. 

(3) Avoid Aatrox’s W Pull - Aatrox W is by far one of his strongest abilities he has, mainly for the reason that his W slow sets up his Q hits. If done right, Aatrox’s W can also instantly cancel your E amid its animation, preventing you from escaping and pulling you back. Make sure to avoid using your E within the last second, using it earlier allows you to escape his potential Q hits as well as his ability to keep you in his range.

(4) Avoid Aatrox’s Passive Auto - Aatrox Passive is another underrated strength in this match up, as it allows him to deal damage based on his target’s maximum HP, while healing him up to 100% of the post mitigation damage dealt. When laning vs Aatrox, make sure to wait for him to use his passive, preventing him the ability to help stat check Renekton within a 1v1. Do note that each time Aatrox uses an auto attack or an ability, he lowers the overall CD of his passive’s 22 to 10 second CD by 2 seconds. If Aatrox hits his Q sweet spots, he’s able to drop the passive CD by 4 seconds for each individual sweet spot he hits. 

(5) Rush Antiheal - It's no secret how crazy Aatrox’s overall healing can be within a fight, so make sure you don’t avoid giving him any chances without grievous wounds. Simply take Ignite or rush an early Executioner’s to lower his overall sustain, as this is a giant powercut to Aatrox's survivability, which affects his passive, Q, Sundered Sky and R interactions. 

(6) Quick Trades - E > Q > AA  > W > AA > E Out / E > Q > W > E - These combos allow for Renekton to get quick damage off in being able to keep health up and whittling his opponent down, use these to get your laner low and look for a low HP kill with flash. 

(7) Play Waves Accordingly - Simply assess whether or not you want to play for freeze, to help you deny XP and CS, while presenting yourself more opportunities to create fights. Or, play to shove waves to create proxy angles, tempo resets or create a dive opportunity. Renekton has all the cards to do whatever he wants with wave management. Also respect that if your laner tries to proxy, simply proxy back or coordinate a kill on them with your jungler. 

(8) Abuse Renekton's R Powerspike - Having Renekton R within this match up essentially allows you to go toe to toe with Aatrox. Aatrox R is a giant powerspike in itself, however the consistent damage from Renekton R on top of the increased fury generation allows you to consistently overpower Aatrox if you're even or ahead. Try to always play around your R for all ins or if Aatrox is threatening an overextended fight.  

(9) Respect Aatrox's R Strength - Aatrox's R increases his attack damage from 20/30/40% AD, and his overall healing by 50/75/100%. Aatrox’s R can be absolutely monstrous in fights, allowing his R to continue an additional 5 seconds for killing enemy champions. When fighting Aatrox, either bait out his R if you want to force it out before teamfights or tower dives, or apply healing reduction against his R if you're committed to the all in.

(10) Build Plated Steelcaps, Eclipse, Black Cleaver or Death's Dance - Go Plated Steelcaps to lower Aatrox's overall damage and to utilise the movement speed vs Aatrox Q / Go Eclipse for consistent power through mid game and damage mitigation with the shield. / Go Black Cleaver for additional CDR and other versatile stats for utility based gameplay. / Go Death's Dance to hard counter Aatrox's Damage and overall healing. 

(11) Midgame + Teamfighting Tips - Within the mid game, Aatrox's spikes are considerably strong in skirmishes and teamfights. Try to lock Aatrox down and protect your carries from him landing his Q's. Aatrox is very easy to shut down in isolation, play off your W and your allies CC to easily shut him down. Before any major objectives, you can also try to catch him out in the side lane. If you’re strong enough to 1v1, make sure to kill him before any major objectives. Or if you have your teammates aside of you, simply focus him down to free up any map pressure he is creating, then look to force fights on his death timer.

column7: The Ahri match up is very difficult due to her ability to easily contest wave pushes, having a mass use of utility to help teammates, and having the ability to easily deny Renekton’s trading patterns. As Renekton we must play around keeping our health up, while playing around our teammates to help get kills on Ahri, or roam the map to help obtain objectives and provide our utility on the map. Make sure to build more defensively and put your ego to the side to put your teammates first. If you try to fight Ahri, make sure to avoid your charm using your E, or look to burst her out and waste her R, providing you and your team more chances to have winning outcomes.
column8:
(1) Level 1 E Start - Try to cheese PTA proc or Conq with E1 > 3 auto's > disengage with E2.

(2) Play For Level 2/3 Kill Angle - Once you chunk out Ahri you're most likely able to kill her with your W, Dash or Flash up. Look to shove the wave around your kill timer, so you're able to make Ahri lose a lot more. 

(3) Play For Sustain Early - Ahri's laning phase is very oppressive early, try to outsustain Ahri through using Empowered Q and abusing D Shield + Second Wind. Make sure to play to keep your HP up, while having the objective to mana burn and cause Ahri to recall. Play for your teammates and item spikes to win and find relevance. 

(3) Avoid Ahri Charm - Ahri Charm is one of the most annoying abilities Renekton can deal with, as she can instantly cancel Renekton E if he engages directly into it. Try to always find ways to creatively bait it out, try to stand behind minions and look to dash or double dash behind her to avoid her charm, or E into her then quickly side step the incoming Ahri charm. Another way is to E in and quickly E out, as this will help you bait out a charm, allowing your teammates access to ganking her. Or with the same method, you can E behind her from E2 in that sequence, to dodge the incoming Ahri charm, allowing you to burn her R or allow you to heavy trade her.  . 

(4) Rush Merc Treads - This is very essential to rush in this match up, as this allows you to have an easier time tanking charms as well as Ahri's overall damage. Having the additional mobility from boots also helps you make faster plays  with E, on top of having the mobility to easily side step her abilities.  

(5) Play For Ganks - Ganks are pretty essential to obtain kills on Ahri. Ahri is a relatively boring statemate lane, so getting ganks from your teammates is going to be crucial in being able to force her out of lane to shove waves and get plates, or simply obtain kill gold in the ability to help you snowball and create a lead within the lane. 

(6) Play Wave On Your Side - Playing the wave on your side essentially means playing wave states on your side of the map, via abusing wave manipulation tactics or freezing on your side of the map. Simply use this to help you combo on your laner, taking away any space from them being able to trade you back (This also helps prevent the enemy running you down with their extended or sustained movement speed abilities). You can also use this wave state to run down your opponent with your abilities up, helping you obtain kills a lot easier vs stalemate or ranged match ups. Look to do this when your opponents are below 50% HP, or potentially make a mistake to provide you an all in opportunity to run them down. 

(7) Play For Teammates - As already mentioned there isn't a lot you can do vs a good Ahri, so simply play around your teammates to help them get in the game. Go towards objectives and try to gank side lanes to make sure you're able to create a gold lead for your own teammates. 

(8) Build Hexdrinker, Eclipse, Stridebreaker or Profane Hydra - Go Hexdrinker to lower Ahri’s overall damage and have a MR shield / Go Eclipse for consistent power through mid game and damage mitigation with the shield. / Go Stridebreaker to cripple Ahri’s mobility and provide teammates with additional utility. / Go Profane for full damage focused playstyles.

(9) Mid Game + Teamfighting Tips - Ahri's objective within the game is to enable her teammates in the ability to catch out her opponents, set up objective based plays, or simply trying to reach the backline and assassinate squishy carries. Renekton's job vs Ahri is to simply protect his teammates from her engages. Try to stun Ahri right away, doing this will lock her in place, allowing you or your teammates to instantly one shot her as fast as you can. Make sure to also tank any Ahri charms once you’re stated enough, as this can be used to peel against her incoming damage for your team.

column7: The Ambessa match up is all about avoiding her main damage, using your range to weave in and out of her abilities, as well as punishing her if she dashes into you. However, a way we can make use of our level 1/2 trades is our ability to force a wave bounce against her. If we are able to crash the 2nd minion wave, then allow her 3rd and 4th wave to push back towards us, this will help us create room to easily force a fight and potentially kill her. Ambessa’s overall weakness is playing in a frozen or extended wave state, taking away her ability to escape to safety. Try to always keep the wave state on your side if you want beneficial trades, as Renekton’s early game completely surpasses Ambessa’s ability to do much. 

(3) Respect Ambessa’s Short Trades - One of Ambessa’s strengths within the Renekton match up is her ability to force short trades. Ambessa’s short trades must be punished or avoided, which Renekton can do within a handful of ways. If Ambessa tries to engage with W, try to utilise your empowered stun immediately onto her shield, as it will instantly break her shield and punish her hard within the process. If Ambessa tries to go for Q trades, try to use your dash to avoid taking her Q damage or use your movement to side step her Q2, to make her lose her additional damage. 

(4) Respect And Avoid Ambessa’s Q - Ambessa’s Q1 allows her to deal damage in a cone, while her Q2 allows her to extend and slam her damage within a line. When fighting Ambessa, try to use your dashes to avoid her Q damage, or look to use your movement to wriggle in and out of her Q positioning. Once Ambessa doesn’t have her Q damage, Renekton can simply brute force a heavy trade onto her, punishing Ambessa’s 14 to 10 seconds Q cooldown. 

(5) Abuse Renekton’s W Shield Break - Renekton’s W can instantly break Ambessa’s shield, allowing her to completely lose out on her ability to mitigate against Renekton’s damage. Try to make sure you’re always holding fury for an empowered W if Ambessa is constantly dashing towards you, as you will be able to easily counter her W as soon as she uses it. 

(6) Play Around Ambessa’s Dashes - Ambessa’s passive allows her to constantly dash after using each ability, providing her with a disgusting amount of mobility through each ability. While this can be annoying, Renekton’s playstyle into Ambessa consists of playing to counter attack her. Each time Ambessa engages on Renekton, Renekton should adequately hold his dashes until she has a limited amount of dashes left. For example, if Ambessa does E > AA > W > AA > Q1 > AA > Q2 Disengage, she will only use her last Q2 to space away against you, allowing you to constantly be in range to use your damage and follow up her Q2 with your own E. Overall, it entirely depends on how Ambessa is using her dashes, but each time she uses an ability it puts each of them on a 10 second + CD earlier on, allowing you to hard punish her back.

(7) Play Wave On Your Side - Playing the wave on your side essentially means playing wave states on your side of the map, via abusing wave manipulation tactics or freezing on your side of the map. You can also use this wave state to run down your opponent with your abilities up, helping you obtain kills a lot easier vs stalemate or ranged match ups. Look to do this when your opponents are below 50% HP, or potentially make a mistake to provide you an all in opportunity to run them down. 

(8) Heavy Trades - Being that Renekton carries a lot of high damage, Renekton is able to just jump on his target nearly at will. column8:
(1) Level 1 Q/E Start - When playing vs Jax level 1, the lane can go two different ways. Jax can either come out of bushes and force a hard trade with Lethal Tempo, or he can start hitting the wave for his grasp, following with him forcing a grasp trade with his E. As Renekton, we need to play accordingly into his play pattern, as we can prevent Jax getting the upper hand early. If Jax has lethal tempo, or if he simply tries to come out of the bush and force his auto attack and E trades, try to skill E and simply dash out of it. Doing this prevents Jax from getting his stun off, as well as being able to proc his auto attacks. Following this scenario, simply wait for him to shove the wave and play for level 2/3 to obtain lane control. 

If Jax doesn’t cheese from the bushes, you can walk into the middle of the lane and take Q start. Jax in this situation most likely will have grasp, meaning he will try to auto the wave then look for his trade with his grasp auto and E. Renekton with Q start can simply overpower Jax, in his ability to poke him down and push for level 2 faster than he can. Do note that spacing plays a GIANT part in avoiding Jax’s early power; make sure to Q right at the edge of your indicator to hit him, try to trade short and play to push with Q, try to also kite jax into a position where your minions will attack him after his E. As long as you preserve HP and reach level 2 before him you essentially win and gain lane control. 

(2) Play Around Jax Passive / Avoid Extended Trades - Jax’s passive is a core component to play around in the match up, as misplaying into his passive will leverage Jax the strength he needs to win every trade and fight vs Renekton. Usually Jax looks to stack passive on a pushing wave, followed by him comboing you if you walk up into his range. The trick to playing around Jax to avoid this, is to always pay attention to his passive stacks. Simply if Jax has passive stacks, don’t fight and just use E to escape his Q engage combo. If Jax doesn’t have stacks, make sure to sit on the wave and punish him if he comes close. Wait out his E, then look to punish him with your combo and E2 out. Furthermore, look to do your trades once your wave starts to slow push from your side; this is beneficial as you’re closer to your side of the map, preventing jax from overstacking passive and allowing for extended trades. 

(3) Respect And Outplay Jax E - Jax E is a giant counter towards Renekton, as he can completely avoid Renekton’s damage and stun, making it a giant power move in 1v1’s. Jax’s E is 17 seconds rank 1 CD, which is crucial for remembering within the match up. If Jax opens up with E you then have 17 seconds afterwards to punish Jax, make sure to hard combo him then look to disengage right after. Sometimes Jax won’t open up with E, in which he will use it mid trade of his combo. If he does this, you can try to time your W right away and disengage if he’s constantly trading with this pattern. 

Sometimes when E’ing away, Jax will also try to E > Q onto your E1 or E2 to try and chase up towards you. Make sure when dashing from Jax E, you hold E2 until he uses his Q animation, as doing this will escape his E stun and also allow you to maintain HP. Also make sure to always hold your W until you know what pattern he is doing, as this is a core way of understanding how to effectively use it. 

(4) W Stun Buffer Vs Jax E - I thought it would also be worth mentioning that you can actually stun Jax E, however you need to have giant balls to do this as it’s very risky in nature. Right at the end of Jax’s E frame, you can right click right at the end of it, to actually stun and deal all 3 of your W hits back at Jax, allowing you to stun him and punish his E. The great thing about this, is that you can ALWAYS do this, as long as Jax uses his E for the full 2 seconds. Problem is Jax can recast his E a second earlier, making this a very risky read unless he is fully committing, where he will use E for every second he can. Use this knowledge wisely and outplay with caution. 

(5) Abuse Empowered Q/E - Playing off your Empowered Q and E are essentially for a lot of portions of the game. As W’ing is hard until Jax E’s, we must rely on using our Q to poke down Jax, allowing us to outsustain and steadily get his HP down. Using Q like this will force Jax into recalling, or leave him troubled under his tower against Renekton’s quick Q waveclear. Later on in the game, Jax R is absolutely disgusting with his overall armour stacking, in which using empowered E to shred a giant portion of that is important for 1v1’ing, or playing around our team when playing vs Jax.   

(6) Play Wave On Your Side - Playing wave on our side is very important vs Jax as it provides safety in nullifying Jax’s extended trades, as well as giving us the perfect room to trade into Jax. Use this side of the map to abuse slow pushes, then wait out until Jax pushes back in order to force him back on your side of the map.

(7) Avoid Fighting Jax R - NEVER FIGHT JAX R. Simply as that, this ability has been buffed and it provides him an insane amount of stats and damage in a pure 1v1. Try to utilise your double dashes to completely escape his all in, as burning his R is a giant resource to allow you to handle him within the lane. Alternatively, we can use empowered E to shred his R if it’s a winnable fight, however this isn’t always consistent as an option, so make sure to assess wisely. 

(8) Abuse Renekton R Powerspike - This is practically always needed vs Jax post 6, as our own stats can help us completely stat check Jax if we’re already ahead, or if we played well enough in an even state. Jax R is still to be avoided in a pure 1v1, however Renekton R can turn the fight if you’re kiting out and playing with minions or ignite to win the 1v1.

(9) Build Eclipse, Black Cleaver or Stridebreaker - Go Eclipse for consistent power through mid game and damage mitigation with the shield. / Go Black Cleaver for additional CDR and other versatile stats for utility based gameplay. / Go Stridebreaker to cripple Jax’s mobility and provide teammates with additional utility.

(10) Mid Game + Teamfighting Tips - Within the mid game, Jax’s overall power level reaches a critical mass when it comes to side laning power, meaning our full attention to fight or trade with Jax is simply non-existent. Once Jax gets Triforce and Sunderered, he can essentially hard win 90% of 1v1’s with Renekton if he has R up, as his low CDs and hard hybrid damage completely gaps Renekton in side lane. With that said, our only role is trying to wave clear and look for plays with our team when he’s isolated. Shutting down Jax is a giant advantage on the map, as he is not able to split push turrets and you’re able to roam or fight for map based objectives. Renekton’s overall strength over Jax is his skirmishing and teamfighting power, so finding opportunities to snowball is essential for beating Jax.

Within teamfights try to either focus Jax’s carries if you’re fed enough to kill them and tank their damage, or play to protect your carries from Jax’s engage with your empowered W’s and your empowered E shred.

(2) Play For Level 2/3 Kill Angle - Once you chunk out Lux you're most likely able to kill her with your W, Dash or Flash up. Look to shove the wave around your kill timer, so you're able to make Lux lose a lot more. 

(3) Respect Lux Poke - Lux’s damage at all points in the game can always hurt, as her ability to easily apply her E, as well as follow up with her Q and passive damage, allows her to deal a lot of damage towards her targets. Being hit by Lux’s stun is usually a death sentence post 6, due to how ridiculous Lux’s damage is. To play vs Lux, we can opt into going D Shield and Second Wind to sustain against her damage if we want to play safe. Lux’s abilities are also pretty easy to avoid, as they’re used within a predictable manner. To easily avoid her abilities, try to use short clicks to move in and out of range, meaning if you’re walking up to her or minions, make sure to click back or to side step any incoming abilities. Once Lux misses her Q or E, Renekton can look to heavily trade against her, forcing a kill or forcing her to recall and waste summoners. 

(4) Avoid Lux Q - Lux’s Q allows her to chain all her damage together, making it a critical ability to always avoid. As previously mentioned, we can use our clicking ability to side step Lux’s Q, although if we’re slowed by Lux’s E or any other abilities, Lux’s ability to land her Q becomes a lot easier. If we’re in situations where we cannot dodge Lux’s incoming Q, we should always try to E instantly out of the way, otherwise Lux will potentially one shot us depending on how strong she is. Within the lane, we can also use our dashes to dodge her incoming Q, allowing us to easily reach her and kill her at will. If we play creatively with our E, we can try to use our E as soon as Lux walks into range of last hitting a minion, or we can face our character’s position away, then use our E to quickly double dash behind her. When dashing in this manner, you’re able to avoid Lux’s incoming Q, as she will most likely mistime her ability to use Q, allowing you to land on top of her and easily out damage her.

(5) Play Wave On Your Side - Playing the wave on your side essentially means playing wave states on your side of the map, via abusing wave manipulation tactics or freezing on your side of the map. Simply use this to help you combo on your laner, taking away any space from them being able to trade you back (This also helps prevent the enemy running you down with their extended or sustained movement speed abilities). You can also use this wave state to run down your opponent with your abilities up, helping you obtain kills a lot easier vs stalemate or ranged match ups. Look to do this when your opponents are below 50% HP, or potentially make a mistake to provide you an all in opportunity to run them down. 

(6) Heavy Trades - Being that Renekton carries a lot of high damage, Renekton is able to just jump on his target nearly at will. Whenever your laners present you with the ability to jump on them, simply take the opportunity to burst them as much as you can. If you didn't kill them already from that, use your options of freezing or your tower diving ability to help you finish off your opponent.

(7) Ping Lux Roams - Lux’s main focus of snowballing against Renekton, is using her roam timers to roam towards side lanes, allowing her to easily use her R to snipe any low HP targets. Typically Lux can easily get kills without hard roaming towards one lane because of her long range R, allowing her to half commit to a roam. To combat her roaming ability, try to spam ping Lux’s whereabouts if she goes missing to help notify her current status. Renekton’s wave clear can also help keep her from roaming in the lane, or it can help punish Lux if she tries to roam. 

(8) Avoid Lux R - As previously mentioned, Lux’s high damage from her R and the rest of her abilities can allow her to instantly delete people from the game. Lux will typically try to land Q > E > R to secure a one shot combo, which she can also use within the fog of war or behind walls, allowing her to easily kill people from mid to high range. Try to always avoid Lux’s combos at all costs, make sure to also use blue trinkets or well placed wards to help track her movements and avoid being caught by her.

(9) Build Mercury Treads, Eclipse, Stridebreaker or Profane - Go Mercury Treads to lower Lux’s overall damage and CC duration. Go Eclipse for consistent power through mid game and damage mitigation with the shield. / Go Stridebreaker to cripple Lux's mobility and provide teammates with additional utility. / Go Profane for full damage focused playstyles.

(10) Mid Game + Teamfighting Tips - Lux’s overall role within the mid to late game, is looking for picks with the use of her medium to high range abilities, allowing her to instantly delete targets to create opportunities to take objectives. Playing against Lux in solo queue is typically harder than it should be, due to them easily ignoring fog of war points while aimlessly walking towards her without a care in the world. Most of the time, we need to play with the intent of keeping Lux away from our team, or at least spotting her on vision before she’s able to get in range of her team. Using wards to spot her out, or crashing side lanes to help force her to take over is generally advised to keep her occupied. When playing against Lux, we should also try to assassinate her on her roam timers. Once we hard push side lane, we can look to camp her jungle and make sure we can assassinate her before she’s able to rotate towards her team. Within team fights, we should try to avoid being in the line of fire of Lux’s abilities, allowing us to keep our HP up and avoid being bursted down by Lux. Try to look to jump on her with our dashes or flash, then use our high damage combos to help burst her down out of the fight. Once Killing Lux, her team will lose out on a lot of utility and range to help poke her enemies down.

column7: Malphite can be either a very easy or difficult match up, as mainly it depends on his playstyle and how Malphite plays. Comet Malphite for instance is a lot easier to deal with as Renekton, as Malphite cannot force constant trades with his early mana issues, which is also countered by Renekton having Second Wind or Doran's Shield. Grasp Malphite on the other hand can go toe to toe with Renekton, forcing Renekton to play more conservatively until Malphite makes a mistake with his abilities. The whole goal of this match up is simply trying to obtain a giant CS lead over malphite, via clearing standard waves or proxying behind his turret when applicable, or trying to freeze on your side of the map, forcing Malphite to waste mana to break the freeze, or allowing Renekton the ability to fight back under his own conditions. Malphite eventually will become a lot more annoying to deal with, hence why Black Cleaver and Empowered E are vital tools when trying to duel or deal with Malphite within teamfights. Do note that as soon as Malphite his E on you, try to just disengage and don't bother trading auto attacks until the E wears off you. Try to also spam ping Malphite's R and try not to clump up together within major objectives, otherwise Malphite R can win him and his team the entire game.
column8:
(1) Level 1 Q Start - Starting Q against Malphite, allows you to easily shove the wave into your level 2 spike, allowing you to hard trade against Malphite by taking E or W. Playing for 2 wave crash into wave bounce is typically how you want to lane against Malphite, as you’re able to lower his HP, then look towards freezing and finding a level 3/4 kill. 

(2) Respect Malphite Q - Malphite’s Q damage depends on his overall build, as if he takes Grasp his overall damage against targets with Q is severely weaker compared to his Comet keystone. If Malphite takes Comet, Malphite will try to hard poke you every time he has his Q and manaflow band up, presenting in really disgusting and heavy damage until he’s able to try and secure a kill onto you. The way to counter this playstyle before entering the game is taking Second Wind, as once you load into the game you can buy Doran Shield against him if he has Comet. Malphite cannot out damage Renekton’s outsustaining power, forcing Malphite to waste a lot of mana and setting himself up for an early Renekton kill.

(3) Respect Malphite W - Malphite’s W allows his next auto attack to become empowered, dealing high physical damage on his first auto and slightly lower increased damage on his remaining hits. Whenever Malphite uses W, we want to avoid trying to trade deeply with him, as Malphite’s auto attacks hurt an absolute ton in combination with his attack speed slow on E. Try to always disengage from Malphite if he uses his W and E onto you, providing you the ability to keep your HP up and our plan to mana burn Malphite. 

(4) Avoid Malphite E - One of the most common reasons Malphite is able to out damage Renekton, is based around the fact people try to fight Malphite while they are attack speed slowed. Malphite’s E slows from 30% to 50% attack speed, which can stack multiplicatively with Frozen Heart’s 20%. Overall Malphite’s ability to negate our total attack speed, prevents us from being able to trade auto attacks against him. There are two ways we can play around Malphite’s E; we can either use short clicks to walk in and out and bait him to cast his E if we walk into his range, or we can use only our abilities to trade, using our E2 to instantly escape fighting him. The overall objective with these types of trades into malphite, is to allow ourselves to easily burn his mana, providing the ability to look for an all in or force him to base. 

(5) Play For Manaburn - As I recently mentioned, playing for mana burn is our most viable way of sustaining a lead over Malphite. Malphite naturally counters our ability to snowball over him, due to his high armour stacking and his annoying mechanics that lower our overall ability to obtain kills over him. Using our techniques of Doran’s Shield and Second Wind, short movements to bait abilities and using our short combos to bait out any abilities of his, will provide us with the result of easily wasting his mana, allowing us to force his recalls to help proxy, take plates or crash minion waves. Don’t try to aim for the kill in this lane, aim to have a high CS lead, as well as removing his mana and presence as a result. 

(6) Play Waves Accordingly - Simply assess whether or not you want to play for freeze, to help you deny XP and CS, while presenting yourself more opportunities to create fights. Or, play to shove waves to create proxy angles, tempo resets or create a dive opportunity. Renekton has all the cards to do whatever he wants with wave management. Also respect that if your laner tries to  proxy, simply proxy back or coordinate a kill on them with your jungler.

(7) Abuse Renekton Empowered E - Renekton’s Empowered E allows him to help shred Malphite’s total armour, synergising with Black Cleaver to help take away Malphite’s unkillable Aura. As the game progresses, using Empowered E is 100% essential for taking away his armour within teamfights. Having the ability to remove 300+ Armour is absolutely crazy value for Renekton, hence why using this is always super important for you and your teammates.

(8) Abuse Renekton’s R Powerspike - Whenever you’re trying to fight Malphite, you must always have your R available if you want to provide that outcome. Renekton’s R magic damage combined with his armour shred and high AD damage, allows him to find early kills on Malphite as long as he plays it well. Malphite can always hold his own within 1v1’s, allowing him to get over confident against Renekton’s R, eventually losing the fight or wasting his R. If you manage to take away Malphite’s R, that’s always a win for you and your team, so make sure to notify your team whenever he doesn’t have it.

(9) Respect Malphite R - Malphite’s R is an absolutely giant play making tool, allowing him to win an entire fight alone from the overall utility or high damage it can provide. Typically, we want to always avoid fights that are held within choke points, as it will easily provide the potential for a 5 man knock up with how tight the terrain is. Try to always avoid fighting Malphite clumped up, make sure to spread out and protect the ulted target if you have the chance to. Otherwise as previously mentioned, try to find ways to force his ults in a 1v1, then look to find a skirmish or teamfight while he has his R down. 

(10) Build Hexdrinker, Eclipse, or Black Cleaver - Go Hexdrinker to lower Malphite’s overall damage and have a MR shield. /  Go Eclipse for consistent power through mid game and damage mitigation with the shield. Go Black Cleaver to hard counter Malphite, allowing you to easily fight and apply armour shred for yourself and the rest of your team.

(11) Mid Game + Teamfighting Tips - Malphite’s playstyle within the mid to late game, consists of stacking heavy armour to counter any AD threats, as well as using his R as a big initiation tool to help him catch out his main targets. Malphite’s overall presence is always annoying to deal with as Renekton, as he’s able to easily access anyone in the game with his R, while he’s practically nearly unkillable if he’s drafted into a heavy AD comp. When playing against Malphite, typically we want to make sure he’s away from our teammates at all costs, meaning we want to hard crash waves on his side of the map. Keeping Malphite away from your team is priority, allowing you to also look for fights with your R and Black Cleaver powerspike, forcing Malphite to potentially waste ult for any upcoming objectives. Whenever you get rid of his R, you’re able to force objectives or fights with your team, as naturally you will be able to make more play making opportunities than Malphite can within a fight. Within teamfights, try to ignore Malphite unless he’s the last target left. Killing Malphite is just a waste of time, so make sure to focus his carries and remove them from the game. When you’re forced to fight Malphite, make sure to use your empowered E to shred his abundance of armour, as well as stacking your Black Cleaver to allow all your teammates to do additional damage against the Malphite.

As Renekton, if you start Q into Riven, she will easily be able to out damage and look for a level 1 kill. Try to respect this as much as possible by letting her take wave control and playing for wave bounce, or skill W and look to be more aggressive.  

(2) Level 1 W Start - Renekton’s hidden tool to beating Riven’s level 1 cheese is actually skilling his W. Renekton W allows you to kill Riven on your second W trade, always presenting a free kill and a giant advantage vs ignite Riven players. Level 1, if Riven goes into to do AA > Q > AA > Q > AA > Q > AA, simply kite back with auto attacks into your minion wave, look to hit her boneplating with auto attacks, then right on the Q3 timing, use your W at the same time as her Q3 frame. Once doing this, kite back towards your tower and stop trading vs Riven. Wait until your next W, which will have enough fury to be empowered. Once W is up, walk back into Riven and use Empowered W and Ignite to kill Riven and win the fight.

(3) Play For Level 2/3 Kill Angle - Once you chunk out Riven you're most likely able to kill her with your W, Dash or Flash up. Look to shove the wave around your kill timer, so you're able to make Riven lose a lot more. 

(4) Abuse Renekton's Early Game - Abuse Renekton's Early Game - In this match up Renekton is essentially able to do whatever he simply wants. With that said, really hone into your strong early to mid game strengths to help you dominate and win the game. Play to deny your enemy of gold and xp, play to proxy and generally lead any top side skirmishes with your insane lane advantage.

These combos can amount to Riven poking down her opponents, with the ability of trying to flash one shot if her target is low enough. When playing vs Riven, we can easily bait out the combo with feints, using our short clicks to move in and out to bait her reactionary combo. Once she slightly falls out of range, missing her W stun, we can abuse this with a heavy trade and look to all in Riven. 

(7) Abuse Renekton W Shield Break - With Riven’s high haste playstyle, she can consistently use her E to mitigate against damage and use it to disengage in any bad situations. A giant counter overall to Riven, is the fact she is unable to keep her HP up vs Renekton as he can easily nuke her shield at will, allowing for easy 1v1’s or tower dives.

(8) Abuse Renekton Attack Buffering - Renekton’s advantage vs Riven is also his ability to use attack buffering through her CC, allowing him to auto attack through her W or Q3. Auto attack buffering can be hard at times, but simply need to spam click on the right frame of her CC to allow you to buffer the auto attack. It should be said that using W is a lot easier with this, as you’re able to consistently trade stuns with Riven, through her W and Q3. This trick is also what helps massively through her level 1 fight, so make sure to abuse these timing points to gain the upper hand vs Riven.

(9) Play Wave On Your Side - Playing the wave on your side essentially means playing wave states on your side of the map, via abusing wave manipulation tactics or freezing on your side of the map. Simply use this to help you combo on your laner, taking away any space from them being able to trade you back (This also helps prevent the enemy running you down with their extended or sustained movement speed abilities). You can also use this wave state to run down your opponent with your abilities up, helping you obtain kills a lot easier vs stalemate or ranged match ups. Look to do this when your opponents are below 50% HP, or potentially make a mistake to provide you an all in opportunity to run them down.

Make sure to always wait for your R CD to help you make plays, otherwise it will lead you towards a major disadvantage in dueling your enemies.

Renekton’s 225% AD Ratio with a 7-4 second CD is simply way too much for Riven to handle. Opting into this playstyle presents the ability to consistently split push and 1v1 Riven, alongside the ability to have constant stuns with W in any teamfights.
